_README: OPTIONAL PANELS. Copy to dashboard.local.json and edit; the .local.json is gitignored
and never leaves your machine. An absent file means every optional panel is OFF, which
is the right default for a feature nobody asked for.
steam: tracks Steam wishlist/sale end dates and shows a panel for them. It is a real
feature and a genuinely personal one - it says something about how you spend your time,
which is not a thing a mail triage tool should assume about you. Off unless you turn it
on. Turning it on also needs dashboard/steam_refresh.local.json for age-gated titles.
_elsewhere_senders: OPTIONAL. Leave this out and the tool decides by SHAPE: mail from an unrepliable
address (no-reply, notifications, alerts) whose subject says a person wanted you.
That works for platforms nobody has heard of, which is the point.
Set it to an exact list of sender substrings if your workplace runs something the
shape test misses, or if the shape test is picking up mail you do not consider a
chat platform. A list REPLACES the shape test rather than adding to it.
